### problem_chain

### task_independent_derivation

**Who, what, when, and on whose authority.** `user_scenario`: Marla Fenwick, workplace operations, Greyfriar Analytics Group.
She states her need in her first sentence — she wants the corporate catering agreement **ended**, today, "as of this call", with the
closing figure "put onto a final bill". She states her authority explicitly ("she is authorised to end the agreement for the firm…
she is the one who signs"). She does **not** want a quote to consider ("She does not want a figure to take away and think about").
She asks for the closing figure to be "put on the account". Object, timing, authorisation mode and terminal state are all unambiguous.

**The customer raises only the root problem.** She never names an invoice, an order, a delivery or any prerequisite. The one sentence
that touches it is purely reactive and conditioned on the agent speaking first: *"If the agent explains that something on the account
has to be written up before the account can be ended, she tells them to go ahead and do it."* She names no other item of work —
no document to send, no address, no statement to raise — beyond the closing figure that `evaluation_criteria` is expected to cover.
She closes where the work closes ("once it comes back confirmed she says that is all she needed"). ✔

**No second reading.** The nearest alternative candidates and the evidence that excludes each:

- *Close first and invoice after* — excluded by the root policy's own sentence "The closing figure is not fixed until every order

- *Close without invoicing at all* — same sentence; and it produces 27618.25, a different scored value.
- *Charge the full service charge on the invoice (789.64)* — excluded by "Where the client holds a cafe contract at the agreement's
  delivery site that stands open and whose service model takes catering out of that kitchen, no service charge is raised", with
  `cafe_contracts[…].status = "active"` and `Full Service Cafe → catering_from_cafe_enabled = true`.
- *Use the base ninety-day spend window (2100.00 → no volume step)* — excluded because that base sentence is declared superseded in
  `catering_ext_delivered_order_invoicing.overwrite[0]`, and the extended rule states the 3/6/12-month ladder.
- *Refuse for want of 45 days' notice* — excluded because that base sentence is declared superseded in
  `catering_ext_agreement_closure_settlement.overwrite[1]`, which prices it as an early-exit charge instead.
- *Waive the shortfall entirely* — excluded because the relief tier needs `counted_spend ≥ 23625.00`; it is 17842.65.

| `standing_round_delivery_charge` | `parameter` — tiers select 0 / half / whole of `delivery_fee_usd` | none (standing round) | eight deliveries in the twelve months ending 2026-03-12, all to `CS-244` = the agreement's `delivery_site_code` | "The delivery charge is the fee printed against the catering service level, raised once for the order." → 55.00 | yes (`P('delivery_fee_usd')`) | **6222.65** | **yes** (+55.00) |

- Whole-baseline fall-back: **6534.99**, a definite number, different from 6167.65. ✔
- `baseline.rule` self-sufficiency: a reader computes 5860 × (100 − 3.00)/100 = 5684.20, + 14 % service charge 795.79, + 0 rush,
  + 55.00 delivery = 6534.99 — definite, and wrong. ✔
- No stamp: no field of any row names "entry volume step", "no service charge", "half rush" or "standing round"; every tier is
  reached through a history aggregate, a date span or the cross-category row.
- **Near-miss**: `catering_orders` row `catering_order_delivered` for `CO-706551`, posted **2025-08-13**. MONTHS(2025-08-13 →
  2026-03-12) = 6, and the six-month window of the rush ladder admits only `0 ≤ m < 6`, so it is excluded by one day. A careless
  reader counts six recent deliveries instead of five. Excluded by the rule sentence "…in the six months ending on the day the invoice
  is raised". A second boundary record: the `catering_order_invoiced` row of 2025-12-04 sits at exactly 3 months and is excluded from
  the baseline window while included in the 12-month one.
- Counts: 5 factors (inside 4–6), 4 `parameter` (≥2), 1 `method` (≥1), all five surviving the tests above.

## findings

**T0-F1 — `SOURCE-FACTOR RED`: a false counterfactual in the proof of `standing_round_delivery_charge`'s weight.**

- **Verdict.** Red light, narrow: the relationship the sentence supports is in fact true, but the sentence asserting it is false and
  is part of the proof the artifact submits.
- **Symptom.** `design_rationale`, "WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS": *"Remove the entries of 2025-04-18 to 2025-08-15 and the
  twelve-month invoiced spend falls below five thousand dollars, so the volume step becomes none; **remove three of the deliveries and
  the delivery charge returns at 55.00**."*
- **Root cause.** The counterfactual was written against the wrong tier boundary. `delivery_count` is **8** in the twelve months
  ending 2026-03-12 (deliveries of 2025-04-15, 2025-06-25, 2025-08-13, 2025-10-07, 2025-12-02, 2026-01-21, 2026-02-11, 2026-03-06).
  Removing three leaves **5**, which still satisfies `standing_round_deliveries = 5` and still selects "no delivery charge at all".
  The full 55.00 fee requires `delivery_count < 2` — seven deliveries would have to go; removing four to seven gives the **half** fee
  of 27.50, never 55.00.
- **Evidence.** `tasks/0.json` `design_rationale` (paragraph quoted above); `initial_state.catering_orders` (the eight
  `catering_order_delivered` rows listed above); `catering.extended.yaml`
  `extended_policies[catering_ext_delivered_order_invoicing].compute[delivery_fee_charged]` and `params.standing_round_deliveries = 5`,
  `params.occasional_round_deliveries = 2`.
- **Demonstrated consequence.** Recomputing on the world the sentence names for itself (eight deliveries less three) gives
  `delivery_fee_charged = 0.00` and an invoice of 6167.65 — unchanged — not the 55.00 the sentence asserts. The proof sentence
  contradicts the recomputation under the relationship "factors bear weight". (The first half of the same sentence, about the volume
  step, **is** correct: 9980.00 − 1620.00 − 1340.00 − 2050.00 = 4970.00 < 5000.00.)
- **Affected artifact.** `env/env_0013_workplace_dining_and_catering_provider/tasks/catering_order_desk/tasks/0.json`,
  `design_rationale`, section "WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS".
- **Relation to previous revisions.** First revision of this audit; no prior revision exists.

**T0-O1 — observation: the closing computation carries no window near-miss.**

- **Symptom.** Every window `catering_ext_agreement_closure_settlement` uses is twelve months, and the earliest row anywhere in this
  task's world is `catering_order_placed` of 2025-04-10 — eleven months before `frozen_time`. No record is excluded from any of that
  computation's aggregates by a window, a channel or a qualifying date.
- **Why an observation.** A trap does exist, but it is by event family rather than by window: `catering_order_cancelled` rows carry
  `charge_code = "cancellation_fee"` (2900.00 on `CO-707930`, 1960.00 on `CO-714462`) exactly as the
  `catering_cancellation_fee_posted` rows do (1450.00, 980.00), so a reader who filters `cancel_charges_12m` by `charge_code` adds
  4860.00 of phantom charges to `counted_spend` and lands on a different shortfall. That is a genuine "careless reader counts it, the
  rule excludes it" record, so the requirement is met — but it is met weakly, and the invoicing computation on the same task carries
  the real thing (the delivery of 2025-08-13, excluded from the six-month rush window by one day).
- **Evidence.** `initial_state.catering_orders` rows of 2025-09-12 and 2026-01-08 (both families, both `charge_code =
  "cancellation_fee"`); `blueprint/db_schema.json` `catering_orders.charge_code`; `catering.extended.yaml`
  `extended_policies[catering_ext_agreement_closure_settlement].compute[cancel_charges_12m]` (filters on `event_type`, not
  `charge_code`).
- **No demonstrated consequence**, so this is not a red light.

**T0-O2 — observation: `LATEST`-scoped object identification.**

- **Symptom.** `catering_ext_delivered_order_invoicing.compute` identifies the order to invoice as
  `LATEST('catering_orders', …, event_type='catering_order_delivered')` — the most recent delivery **on the agreement** — with no
  filter on `order_reference`, while the rule speaks of "a catering order that has been served".
- **Why an observation.** On this world the most recent delivery is the only delivered-and-uninvoiced order, so the two coincide and
  the scored value is unaffected. It is recorded because the coincidence is a property of the seed rather than of the policy: a world
  with two uninvoiced deliveries would make the policy pick the later one silently.
- **Evidence.** `catering.extended.yaml` `extended_policies[0].compute[served_value]`, `[served_date]`, `[served_site]`;
  `initial_state.catering_orders` (only `CO-719044` is delivered and uninvoiced).

- **T0-O2** — answered as a property of this world (the `LATEST` delivery is the only delivered-and-uninvoiced order) rather than a
  defect; narrowing the binding would change the policy, not the task. Accepted.
- **O-4** — answered as inherited but unimplementable, unable to produce a competing write. Accepted.

Relation to previous revisions: revision 1's single red light against this task is resolved; no revision-1 PASS regressed.

`### sibling 3 — the cafe parameter in the cafe corpus's words`, `### face sweep, re-run by this audit` and
`## findings (revision 4)`.

This task carried no red light out of revision 3 and none out of the render-layer audit. The question here is again:
**was it disturbed?** — and this round, unlike round 3, the change reaching it is a change to its own rule text.

## what reached this task, and what it cost

Both of this task's policies had **the same cross-product vocabulary hazard on their cafe read** as task 1 had on its banquet read,
and both were corrected. This was not a cosmetic copy of task 1's fix:

| | round 3 wording | round 4 wording | why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cafe state | "a cafe contract … that **stands open**" | "a cafe contract … that **stands active**" | `docs/cafe/` says "stands active" throughout, contrasting it with suspended, in transition out, mobilizing, proposed and closed; it never uses "open" of a cafe contract's own state |
| cafe parameter | "whose service model **takes catering out of that kitchen**" | "whose service model **permits catering to be ordered out of that kitchen**" | zero occurrences of the retired phrase in `docs/cafe/`; the cafe corpus prints the parameter as "whether catering may be ordered out of the cafe kitchen", column "Catering from the cafe kitchen" |

Both changes moved on **every face together** — `rule`, `baseline.rule` where it carries the sentence, `compute_basis`, the
`cross_category` note, and each ladder tier condition — and both tier conditions of `kitchen_service_concession` and of
`programme_spend_benchmark` remain **verbatim substrings** of their own policy's rule, tested by exact containment.

**The "stands open" defect had teeth on this task's policies, though not on this task's world.** The cafe lifecycle is
`proposed, mobilizing, active, suspended, in_transition_out, closed`. A reader taking "open" as "not closed" admits three states the
compute (`cafe_status == 'active'`) excludes, so the round-3 rule promised a tier the compute never produces. It also collided with a
live base sentence — `catering_combination_cafe_interaction`'s *"Where the cafe contract at the delivery site stands suspended,
catering out of that kitchen stops with it…"* — which says a suspended cafe must **not** draw the kitchen concession. On this task's
world the seeded cafe contract at `CS-244` stands `active`, so both readings coincided and **no scored value was ever at risk here**;
the defect was in the ladder's domain, not in this world. That is why revision 3 could pass this task and the fix still be right.

Verified for this world against the published cafe corpus rather than against the blueprint alone:
`docs/cafe/service_operations_schedule_5c72f887.json`'s row `| Full Service Cafe | … | Yes | …` under the column
**"Catering from the cafe kitchen"** resolves the new phrase to the same value `CPARAM('cafe','catering_from_cafe_enabled')` reads
(`true` for Full Service Cafe in `blueprint/products/cafe.yaml`). **The tier taken is the same under either wording.**
